🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-09-03 23:00 → 2026-09-04 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **PRF framework caught consistent AI authority failure** — Pavlo's Protected Relation Fixtures ran against a high-reasoning AI model and produced a clean failure signal in all ten blind runs, turning a design boundary into hard evidence. [tg:tawg:4272]

> **Independent cross-gateway verification confirmed consistent results** — Baby Blue Viper rebuilt the check from scratch across two separate gateways and found identical confirmed responses, independently corroborating the verification path. [tg:tawg:4226]

> **Multi-feature release merged to main** — Verification routing, ERC scan registration, and privacy enhancements landed together in tawg-daily-contribution, closing a significant development loop. [PR #13](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/13)

> **TruthAnchor ERCs disambiguated in primitives** — A commit formally separates ERC-8281 from a competing ERC-8263 TruthAnchorV1, clearing a naming collision that could have created confusion across the shared spec. [commit c4ed915](https://github.com/trustless-ai/primitives/commit/c4ed915df3a4a2db7b37ad9819a74af541210f43)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### PRF testing
_The Protected Relation Fixtures framework moved from concept to concrete AI evaluation results._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Introduced** Protected Relation Fixtures, a boundary-based testing layer that distinguishes authority relations even when their outputs are identical, giving the group a principled tool for detecting when an agent conflates structurally different proofs. [tg:tawg:4245]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Clarified** the critical fixture boundary: an authority relation derived from a signed source is categorically different from one authenticated through consensus, even when both produce the same value—and the fixture encodes that distinction explicitly. [tg:tawg:4246]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Validated** the framework against a high-reasoning AI model and found it returned the wrong authority classification in every one of ten independent blind runs, demonstrating that the fixture surfaces real failures that looser tests would not catch. [tg:tawg:4272]

### ERC-8004
_Quantitative evidence and independent verification deepened the group's understanding of the mechanism._

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Verified** independently and from scratch that two separate gateway endpoints return matching confirmed responses, establishing cross-gateway consistency without relying on any prior report. [tg:tawg:4226]
- A contributor on Ethereum Magicians confirmed structural room for the proposed mechanism, establishing a baseline that the subsequent quantitative work could build on. [Magicians #390](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/390)
- Baby Blue Viper **Reframed** the discussion by surfacing that the meaningful finding is the ~62–67% divergence range rather than a structural yes, sharpening what the mechanism actually demonstrates for ERC-8004. [Magicians #391](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/391)

### tawg-daily-contribution
_A multi-feature development release reached the main branch._

- Jimmy Shi **Shipped** a dev-to-main release combining verification routing, ERC scan registration, and privacy enhancements, consolidating accumulated development work and making the full updated feature set available to the group. [PR #13](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/13)

### primitives
_The TruthAnchor naming ambiguity between two ERCs was resolved in the shared repository._

- Merlini **Committed** a disambiguation separating ERC-8281 (the group's TruthAnchor) from an external ERC-8263 TruthAnchorV1 and added Attestation context, removing a name collision that could have caused cross-ERC confusion in the shared spec. [commit c4ed915](https://github.com/trustless-ai/primitives/commit/c4ed915df3a4a2db7b37ad9819a74af541210f43)

### agent-contracts-examples
_Both mainnet deployments reached Sourcify verification status._

- Merlini **Updated** the genesis-self-source README to list both mainnet deployments with their Sourcify verification status, making the deployment state independently verifiable and reinforcing the group's trustless infrastructure goal. [PR #4](https://github.com/trustless-ai/agent-contracts-examples/pull/4)

### signed-events substrate
_A design discussion opened around privacy-preserving signed event tracking for agents._

- Ryan VETEZE (@veteze) **Shared** a substrate design where every agent mention becomes a signed event recording a hashed requester handle with no PII, the responding agent, and content, advancing the group's thinking on accountable and privacy-respecting agent interactions. [tg:tawg:4220]

### cross-reference-console
_Automated tooling kept the claims registry synchronized._

- The cross-reference-console watcher pushed a registry update refreshing the claims watermark, keeping the automated tracking layer current with the latest cross-reference data. [commit 5341a76](https://github.com/trustless-ai/cross-reference-console/commit/5341a76eb33b2e56556d74f8ec5676576c633dda)

### community
_ETHGlobal Lisbon and an open implementation question pointed the group forward._

- Merlini (@gobross) **Shared** the ETHGlobal Lisbon 2026 team page, making the group's ecosystem participation visible and flagging an upcoming venue where Trustless AI work could gain broader exposure. [tg:tawg:4257]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Raised** a practical question about how an agent can reply in Telegram without a dedicated bot account, opening a concrete implementation thread for the group's agent-messaging work. [tg:tawg:4290]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Extend the PRF suite to benchmark additional AI models against the authority-relation boundary
- Follow up on the quantitative divergence finding and explore what mechanism changes would shift the ~62–67% range
- Investigate how the signed-events substrate connects to the cross-gateway verification path as a provenance layer
- Consider what demo or artifact best represents the group's work for ETHGlobal Lisbon 2026

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Investigate how an agent can reply to Telegram messages without a dedicated bot account
- Confirm that Sourcify verification links for both genesis-self-source mainnet deployments are live and accessible
- Review whether the ERC-8281 / ERC-8263 disambiguation needs corresponding updates in any dependent documentation

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** The PRF framework didn't just describe an authority boundary — it ran ten blind trials against a leading AI model and got ten identical failures. Design, fixture, test, clear result, all in one day: that kind of complete loop is exactly what turns shared ideas into shared evidence.
>
> When the thing you built to catch a failure catches it every single time on the very first real run, the design question was definitely the right one. Keep running those fixtures! 🔬
